title: Bike Watching 🚴‍♀️
description: This interactive visualization maps the Bluebikes bikeshare system across Boston and Cambridge. It displays station locations, their usage levels, and bike lane networks, allowing users to explore commuter patterns and popular routes. The time filter reveals how bikeshare usage changes throughout the day, providing insights into urban mobility patterns.

title: Recipe Time Estimator
description: This project aimed to predict the actual cooking time of a recipe, in minutes, based on key recipe attributes such as the number of steps, number of ingredients, and descriptive tags. I worked with a merged dataset of over 230,000 entries from RAW_recipes.csv and interactions.csv, combining recipe details with user ratings and reviews. After extensive data cleaning—including handling missing values, removing duplicates, and correcting data types—I engineered relevant features and performed exploratory data analysis to identify trends and potential predictors of cooking time. This project allowed me to apply regression modeling techniques to a real-world problem, while exploring how recipe complexity and metadata can be used to enhance the accuracy of time estimates for online recipes.

title: California Wildfire Analysis
description: This project explores whether rising average temperatures—driven by climate change—are linked to more severe wildfires, measured by acres burned or damaged, across California counties. I analyzed the California Wildfire Damage Dataset (2014–Feb 2025) to investigate these patterns, inspired by my personal concern for how global warming is intensifying natural disasters. Through this analysis, I aimed to better understand the real-world impacts of climate change in my home state and provide insights that could help inform future prevention and recovery strategies.

title: Deceptive or Honest Data Visualizations?
description: This project compares an honest and a deceptive visualization of the relationship between abortion clinic access and out-of-state travel for abortion care. The honest version uses clear, justifiable design choices—like a logarithmic scale and trendline—to reveal a strong negative correlation. The deceptive version distorts the story through misleading tactics such as a fake trendline, misaligned axes, and cherry-picked data. This highlights how design decisions can either clarify or manipulate data, emphasizing the need for ethical, transparent visual storytelling.

title: T-Race
description: This project visualizes dinosaur data through both static and dynamic visualizations. We began by creating histograms to display the distribution of dinosaur lengths across six major geological eras. Building on this, we developed a bar chart race animation to illustrate how dinosaur fossil counts varied by location over millions of years. The project involved extensive data cleaning, exploratory data analysis, and the use of the bar_chart_race Python package to enhance temporal data storytelling through engaging visualizations.
